subject.title: MissingAgentHarnessError race: non-atomic harness registry clear+restore during plugin cache cycle

question: What harness ownership contract should OpenClaw enforce when plugin reload/startup resolves to an empty active scope?
rationale: The bug is real, but restore-all preservation can keep disabled or unscoped plugin-owned harnesses callable, while unconditional clearing can break active channel or cron turns; the permanent contract is a maintainer product and security boundary decision.

options.title: Preserve only approved always-on harnesses
options.body: Filter restored harnesses to an explicit bundled/always-on contract and prove plugin-owned harnesses clear when their owner is disabled or out of scope.

options.title: Accept restore-all semantics
options.body: Allow previous harnesses to survive empty active registries, but document and test that plugin disablement does not immediately revoke those harnesses.

options.title: Pause for broader lifecycle redesign
options.body: Replace the global mutable registry with an ownership-aware or request-scoped lifecycle model before landing a narrow empty-scope patch.

recommendation.title: Preserve only approved always-on harnesses
recommendation.body: Filter restored harnesses to an explicit bundled/always-on contract and prove plugin-owned harnesses clear when their owner is disabled or out of scope.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the pluggable harness registry and has the strongest path-history signal for the agent-runtime lifecycle contract.
